rules.feature: Time-of-day service: RDS as local-time source
rules.effect: TimeofDayService may take the tuner's RDS clock time as its LOCAL time source when the vehicle's cellular local time is not available. Inside the service, local time is used only to derive a time zone (rounded half-hour difference to trusted time, or to the remote real-time clock when there is none, then AlarmManager.setTimeZone) while auto_time_zone is 1. It never sets the system clock
rules.check: log 'TimeOfDay:GMTuner: computed Local Time' / 'VehicleTime: Setting time zone to'
rules.note: RDS time arrives as a JSON string in the media-session extras of com.gm.gmaudio.tuner, which reads vendor parameter com.gm.rds_time from the broadcast-radio HAL (vendor.harman.tuner-service; strings and symbols name RdsClockTime, sendRdsTime, updateRdsTime; not decompiled). Accepted only when two successive values lie within 180 s and either bit <country code> of PI_CODE_CONFIGURATION is set or it is within RDS_CLOCK_TIME_MAX_DIFF minutes of the system's local clock. rules.feature: Time-of-day service: trusted time applied to the system clock
rules.effect: TimeofDayService starts trusted-time updates and, once a value is verified, sets the remote real-time clock and the system clock from it in BOTH auto_time modes. Settings.Global auto_time (read at service start and on every change) selects only the offset: 1 = the clock is set to trusted time and persist.sys.clockOffset is reset to 0; 0 = the clock is set to trusted time minus persist.sys.clockOffset. false: no trusted-time updates; the clock comes from the remote real-time clock (else 2020-01-01) under the same offset rule
rules.check: log 'VehicleTime: Trusted time verified and locked' / 'VehicleTime: Setting time to'; adb shell getprop persist.sys.clockOffset; adb shell settings get global auto_time
rules.note: No branch on mTimeUpdateMode skips a clock write. updateSystemClock() subtracts the offset in manual mode and sets the clock when it is more than 1.5 s from the target; syncClocks() (first verified trusted time) and calculateDrift() call it in both modes. In manual mode the offset is recomputed at every TIME_SET / DATE_CHANGED as (trusted time, or the remote real-time clock when there is none) minus the system clock, so a manual entry survives later corrections; an offset taken against a wrong remote clock is kept when trusted time arrives. Switching auto_time to 1 sets the clock to trusted time and zeroes the offset; a time set from elsewhere in automatic mode is undone by the next drift check. Drift monitor: a repeating alarm every 30 minutes (1800000 ms; started at boot-completed and resume, stopped on suspend) runs calculateDrift(), which re-sets both clocks when the remote clock is more than 1.5 s or the system clock more than 0.5 s from the expected value. That is a re-check period, not a limit on the size of a correction: this service has no upper bound on how far a trusted time may move the clock. It is unrelated to RDS_CLOCK_TIME_MAX_DIFF (minutes, RDS local time only) and to the half-hour rounding of the time-zone offset (time.rds_local_source). A trusted value is accepted after five further values each within 3 s of the one before, or at once when the first value is within 3 s of the remote clock. BACK_OFFICE_SERVER_ENABLED is not read by this service. Whether a location provider delivers fixes for value 1 on this hardware is unknown.

rules.effect: The full trailering app creates its network connection manager. Once the network is up and the OnStar account reports the TRAILER entitlement, it runs a profile sync and repeats it every 30 minutes: HTTPS requests to https://<ACCOUNT_AUTHENTICATOR_SERVER_NAME>:<SECURITY_EVENT_LOGGING_SERVER_HOST_PORT>/api/v2/trailering/... with a bearer token; request paths carry the VIN and trailer ids, bodies carry trailer profiles, checklists, maintenance reminders, tyre-pressure sensor data and metrics (distance delta, fuel economy, transmission temperature). App type 1 (lite) or 0: the manager is never created
rules.check: logcat 'Backoffice URL  =', 'Trailering Entitlement is AVAILABLE, starting BO', 'Running 30 min Sync'; packet capture
rules.note: trailer_backoffice_allowed: demo mode off, an active network, and an OnStar account that is active with TRAILER entitlement state 1 (or 2 with type Data); without the entitlement no request adapter is built. System property persist.gm.bo.trailer.sync (minutes) replaces the 30-minute period. The client is built with Retrofit log level FULL, whose Android default writes requests and responses to logcat tag Retrofit. Read in code, nothing run: the link from the network check to the VIN event and the individual request builders were not followed line by line. Despite its name, SECURITY_EVENT_LOGGING_SERVER_HOST_PORT has no other reader on the image. TLS: GMTrailer's TrustClient.openConnection() is gm.android.security.GMHttpsConnector(..., GMTrustedGmRootCertificateStore, clientAuth=true, ocsp=true); server cert pinned to the GM root CA, hostname check disabled, so a home-lab redirect of ACCOUNT_AUTHENTICATOR_SERVER_NAME / SECURITY_EVENT_LOGGING_SERVER_HOST_PORT is rejected at the handshake (README 'Network destinations').

rules.effect: GMSubscriptionManager VehicleCalibrationDAO builds the app-shop URL https://<APP_SHOP_SERVER_NAME> (getSalesforceUrl), gated for app-shop use by APP_SHOP_SERVER_ENABLED (isAppShopServerEnabled); the port calibrations APP_SHOP_SERVER_*_HOST_PORT have no reader (the host string carries no port, so HTTPS 443 is used). rules.note: APP_SHOP_SERVER_NAME is read only by GUID here (no string-literal/CalId read site), so it keeps status 'read, effect not traced' even though its effect is traced in this rule; its redirect feasibility is the same GM two-way-auth verdict as the other PAPI destinations.
